mathematical_checks.reason: Exactly one unit denominator and three denominators greater than one make all six pair products strictly positive; integer row/pair data and positive weights are precisely the isolated-vertex lemma hypotheses.

The isolated-vertex proof uses row sums, pair products, integer gaps and the already established cycle-gain criterion, not the three-high matching theorem. A later explanatory remark referring back to matching is not a proof premise.

At an isolated vertex h, c_i=-p_hi>0 and each sum of two integer gaps equals one. Selecting a nonpositive gap at every remaining vertex produces a positive directed cycle whose gain is at least one, contrary to positive weights.
